prompt: Run the LLM ablation baselines llm-skeleton2grid and llm-working2grid for as-twn-kaohsiung-shape-rect (variant orig), model opus5. The model is the optimiser: every grid cell must be reasoned out point by point, not generated by an algorithm.

transcript.note: Round 1. Read the topology first: C (輕軌) is a closed ring 4-11-6-7-14-16-0-3-15-13-4, R runs 1-9-5-3-8-7-2 north to south-east, O runs 4-8-16-10-12 west to east, and 16 is the crossing where O passes through the ring's east side. Criterion 1 (interchanges first): the five degree>=3 points are 3, 4, 7, 8, 16, and every one of them sits on the ring or on the O/R spine, so I pinned the ring as a true rectangle and hung everything else off it. Ring rectangle = left col 0 (11 r4, 4 r6, 13 r7, 15 r9), bottom row 4 (11 c0, 6 c4, 7 c5, 14 c8), right col 8 (14 r4, 16 r6, 0 r9), top row 9 (0 c8, 3 c5, 15 c0) -- all 10 ring segments come out H/V. Criterion 2 (one line one direction): R gets column 5 for its whole trunk, so 7-8, 8-3, 3-5, 5-9 are four verticals stacked in one line, and O gets row 6 for its whole length, so 4-8, 8-16, 16-10, 10-12 are four horizontals; 8 (美麗島) is the point where the two spines cross inside the ring, and it lands on (5,6) because that is col(R) x row(O). 1 (岡山) goes to (3,22) so 9-1 is horizontal and 1 still stays west of 6 (gx 208 < 224) -- putting 1 in column 5 would have made 1-9 vertical too but would have flipped 1 against 6. Only 7-2 (小港) is left off-axis: 2 has to stay east of 10 (gx 683 > 630) and off row 4, otherwise it would either flip against 10 or swallow 14 on the bottom edge. Criterion 3: rows were chosen proportional to real northness (2 -> 0, ring bottom -> 4, O spine -> 6, 13 -> 7, ring top -> 9, 5 -> 14, 1/9 -> 22) and columns proportional to gx, so no east/west or north/south pair is reversed. Criterion 4: the ring is drawn tight (cols 0-8, rows 4-9) because those 10 points really do sit in a compact blob in west Kaohsiung, while the long R stretch up to 岡山 and the long O stretch out to 大寮 keep their real length.
